subject: Chemistry
description: Groups, periods, trends, noble gases, transition metals

questions.stem: The modern periodic table has how many groups (vertical columns)?
questions.explanation: The modern (long-form) periodic table has 18 groups and 7 periods. Mendeleev's original table (1869) had 8 groups. Group 1 — alkali metals; Group 2 — alkaline earth metals; Groups 3-12 — transition metals; Group 17 — halogens; Group 18 — noble gases. Elements in a group have similar chemical properties because they share the same outer-shell electron configuration.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Noble gases are found in which group of the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Group 18: helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, radon, oganesson. Fully filled outer shells make them chemically very stable (inert). Earth's atmosphere is ~1 % argon. Neon is used in red-orange sign lighting; helium in balloons and cryogenics; xenon in car headlamps and arc lamps; radon is radioactive. Group 1 — alkali metals; Group 17 — halogens.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: In the modern periodic table, elements are arranged in order of increasing:
questions.explanation: The modern periodic law (Moseley, 1913) states that properties are a periodic function of atomic number (number of protons), not atomic mass as Mendeleev had assumed. This resolved anomalies — e.g., argon (40) appears before potassium (39) because Ar has atomic number 18 and K has 19, even though Ar's atomic mass is higher. Electronegativity itself is a periodic trend, not the ordering rule.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: As we move left to right across a period, atomic size generally:
questions.explanation: Across a period — nuclear charge grows while electrons are added to the same shell. The stronger pull shrinks the atom. Down a group — electrons go into new shells, so size grows despite the extra charge. That is why Li is smaller than Na (same group) is smaller than K, but larger than Be (same period).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which element is the most electronegative?
questions.explanation: Fluorine (F, atomic number 9) is the most electronegative element on the Pauling scale (3.98). Oxygen is second (3.44), chlorine third (3.16), nitrogen fourth (3.04). Electronegativity increases left-to-right across a period and decreases down a group — which is why F (top of Group 17) beats Cl (below it). Caesium is one of the least electronegative (0.79).

questions.stem: The element with the highest melting point among all naturally-occurring elements is:
questions.explanation: Tungsten — also called wolfram, symbol W — melts at 3,422 °C, the highest of any metal and second only to carbon (sublimes ~3,642 °C) among naturally occurring elements. That is why tungsten is used for incandescent bulb filaments and high-temperature cutting tools. Iron melts at 1,538 °C; gold at 1,064 °C; platinum at 1,768 °C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Dmitri Mendeleev's original periodic table (1869) arranged elements in order of increasing:
questions.explanation: Mendeleev's law (1869) arranged the then-known 63 elements in order of increasing atomic mass — and famously left gaps for elements not yet discovered (eka-aluminium = gallium, eka-boron = scandium, eka-silicon = germanium, all later found). Only in 1913 did Moseley's X-ray work establish that atomic number — not mass — is the true ordering variable.
